source.title: On the Emergence of Invariance and Disentangling in Deep Representations

page_placements.theme: Random-label memorization changes measured information and compression

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests fitting random labels under an explicit information bottleneck regularizer, measuring training error across regularizer strengths; this changes the training method from the original claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for standard CNNs fitting random labels; those cited results are not this study's rows. Its own random-label experiment reports training-error results under the IB regularizer. The label-corruption experiment measures information in weights, not training or test error across corruption levels.
record.test_reason: The study measures random-label training error in three CNN architectures while varying an information bottleneck regularizer. This tests fitting capacity under a changed training objective, with limited applicability to V1's unchanged standard-training setup.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors argue that memorizing random labels requires information in the weights that grows with dataset size. Their computable IB regularizer produces an architecture-consistent transition from complete fitting to underfitting before, and near, the theoretical threshold β = 1.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an explicit information bottleneck regularizer on the weights and sweeps β; it does not reproduce standard unregularized training. The paper describes its setup as similar to Zhang et al. (2017).
record.method_sensitivity: The training-error outcome changes with β; the authors report a phase transition near β = 1 across the tested architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: At β = 0.1 and N = 30,000, estimated information in Small AlexNet's weights increases with label corruption, by approximately 3 nats/sample for fully random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitting more label noise requires more information stored in the weights under the study's information estimate.

record.problems: The random-label training-error results are shown in figures without textual numerical values. The experiments use an explicit regularizer, and no test-error-at-chance result is reported for the random-label experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported random-label training-error results beyond the architecture-by-regularizer rows were identified. The separate label-corruption sweep in Figure 2 (right) measures information in weights, not a V1–V6 outcome that qualifies for a row.

untested.parts: Unchanged standard architecture and training hyperparameters relative to true-label training are not established. The study introduces stochastic weights and an IB penalty; Figure 1 also selects between learning rates. Chance-level test error cannot be quantified from the supplied figure text.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A joint corruption sweep demonstrating perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error. Figure 2's corruption sweep reports information in weights instead.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing those methods preserves true-label generalization. The IB penalty is a different regularizer.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noise.

missing.what: Figure 1 reports the study's own Small AlexNet random-label training and test accuracy across dataset sizes and β. These results extend beyond the 10,000-sample architecture sweep. Its caption explicitly discusses uniformly low random-label test accuracy, so the record's blanket statement that no random-label test result is reported needs correction. Numerical values require the actual figure.
missing.locator: Figure 1 and caption; Section 7.1; Appendix A.1

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Low-β fitting and high-β underfitting warrant separate verdicts. High-β results do not challenge the unchanged standard-training claim. Figure 1 is an additional experiment, not merely a reproduction of a cited result.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments do not test the unregularized standard training setup or test error at chance; they use the IB regularized loss.
Training-time cost relative to true labels and convergence speed across corruption levels are not reported.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The corruption sweep measures information in weights, not whether training error stays perfect or test error rises steadily.
The tested regularizer is the information bottleneck loss, not weight decay, dropout or data augmentation; the paper does not test removing those methods for generalization on true labels.
The paper does not test the order in which real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned.
